title: Plutonium Half-Life and Radioactive Decay
learningObjectives: Use N=N0*(1/2)^(t/T) to calculate the amount of plutonium remaining after a given elapsed time.
Explain that isotopes with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives.
Describe that decaying plutonium isotopes transform into different isotopes or elements.

evidence.quote: The different isotopes have different “half-lives” – the time it takes to lose half of its radioactivity.

explanations.text: Half-life is the time to lose half of the radioactivity, so the remaining amount is halved after each half-life.

evidence.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.
Substances with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives, so they emit more energetic radioactivity.

explanations.text: Pu-239 has a long half-life of 24,100 years while Pu-241 has a short half-life of 14.4 years, and shorter half-lives decay more quickly with more energetic radioactivity.

evidence.quote: Like any radioactive isotopes, plutonium isotopes transform when they decay.

explanations.text: When plutonium isotopes decay they transform, becoming different plutonium isotopes or different elements.

predictions.prompt: A 100 gram sample has a 10-year half-life. How much remains after 5 years?
A 200 gram sample has a 14.4-year half-life. How much remains after 14.4 years?
An 80 gram sample has a 5-year half-life. How much remains after 15 years?
